newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end fractionally higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end fractionally higher.

text.p: French stocks ended fractionally higher on Wednesday, helped by Wall Street's gains, but off their session highs as a stronger-than-expected U.S. industrial production data fanned fears of higher interest rates.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 0.34 point, or 0.01 percent, at 2,620.97, while the CAC-40 futures contract finished down 12 at 2,614.
"Everything's being decided by what's happening in the United States," said a trader, adding investors were watching the Dow index and the dollar.
Wall Street's mid-morning recovery lifted the French market out of negative territory.

* Shares in off-shore engineering company Coflexip fell 2.73 percent to 323.90 francs. CDC Bourse confirmed talk it had carried out a placement of Coflexip shares but gave no details. One fund manager said the shares were placed at 314 francs. Some dealers said re-insurer SCOR was the seller. Officials at SCOR and Coflexip declined comment.
* BIC rose 2.6 percent to 868 francs. On Tuesday night it announced a 13 percent sales rise for the first quarter and proposed a two-for-one stock split for July.
* Pechiney rose 5.17 percent to 217.50 francs as investors were encouraged by the first-quarter results of its U.S. rival Reynolds Metals Co.

* Two blocks totalling 258,000 shares of equipment manufacturer Sommer-Allibert representing just over one percent of its capital were traded, market sources said. They said 208,000 shares were traded at 194.70 francs each, followed by a block of 50,000 priced at 195 francs per share.

* A block of five million Cie de Suez shares, representing 3.05 percent of the capital, was traded off-market on Tuesday evening, the French stockmarkets' association SBF said. The trade was carried out at 285 francs per share.

* Club Mediterranee rose 3.18 percent to 490.10 francs, bolstered by recent management changes by new chief executive Philippe Bourguignon. Some market operators say the stock's recent rise may be overdone.
* PSA Peugeot Citroen shares rose 1.59 percent ahead of the 1996 results due on Thursday morning. The consensus is for net attributable profit of around 1.2 billion francs.
